trust_decision.summary: The panel mints node JWTs signed with one per-node HMAC key and no purpose/scope claim, so Wings cannot tell a download/websocket token from an upload token; the panel decides the permission (file.read vs file.create etc.) per route, but the token it issues does not carry which operation it was minted for. Enforcement of the scope is in Wings (separate repo); the panel's only role is to stamp the scope.

landing_point.why: The summary names subuser file upload and file.create; the upload URL token is minted here.

fix_sites.entry_point: shared token builder called by every route below (adds setScopes, mandatory scope claim; fix.diff:163-168, fix.diff:189-191)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Closest candidate: app/Http/Controllers/Admin/Servers/ServerTransferController.php:78-81 (admin-only node-to-node transfer token), but it is just another caller of the same builder, not one of the listed kinds.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The transfer token is admin-issued, has no user and is node-to-node, so a solver could argue it is unrelated to subuser permissions; likewise the websocket token already carries a permissions claim.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Each legitimate token must still work for its own purpose: the websocket token keeps its permissions/server_uuid/user_uuid claims, the transfer token has no user, and backup restore from S3 uses DownloadLinkService without a JWT. An over-broad fix (e.g. one fixed scope for all tokens, or throwing for user-less tokens) breaks transfer or websocket.

O6_input_shapes: one scope per token (each call site)
variadic list of scopes serialised as a space-separated 'scope' claim (fix.diff:163-168, fix.diff:191)

O7_producer.where: app/Services/Nodes/NodeJWTService.php:68-101 builds and signs the claim set; the consumer that checks the scope is Wings, outside this repository

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second signed-URL action (e.g. a pull/archive download link) minting a NodeJWTService token
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The controller already mints a download URL token next to other file actions; a maintainer adding another signed link would copy this block. Still a WHERE-type sibling: one grep for NodeJWTService finds it.

O9_family: Authorization / token scoping: bearer token missing purpose (audience/scope) binding, which allows privilege confusion between token types (CWE-1259/1270, A01)

O10_build.toolchain: PHP 8.2+ with Composer (composer.json:20), Laravel, lcobucci/jwt ^5.6 (composer.json:36), PHPUnit
O10_build.project_tests: tests/Integration/Api/Client/Server/WebsocketControllerTest.php decodes the minted JWT and checks claims; the fix adds tests/Integration/Services/Backups/DownloadLinkServiceTest.php (not present at pin). Unit tests run with DB_HOST=UNIT_NO_DB (.github/workflows/ci.yaml:55).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a scope/purpose claim only to the upload token (or only upload + download), leaving websocket, backup and transfer tokens unscoped.

out_of_scope_notes: The fix switches the jti hash from md5 to sha256 (fix.diff:177-181), but app/Repositories/Wings/DaemonServerRepository.php:143 still revokes md5($id . uuid), so after the fix revocation of user tokens no longer matches. Not pursued.
The fix also drops the deprecated user_id claim (fix.diff:193-202). That is a compatibility change, not part of the protection.
unverified: The actual scope enforcement lives in Wings (Go, separate repo; GO-2026-6120). Hidden panel-side tests can only check that the claim is present with the right value, and the exact strings ('file-upload', 'file-download', 'websocket', 'backup-download', 'transfer') are an interface contract that a solver cannot infer unless the report states them. This is a fairness problem for task design.
Repo size in MB was not measured (no shell use).
Whether NodeJWTService is container-shared, so builder state such as claims/user leaks between calls, was not checked; Laravel default is a fresh instance per resolution.
